situation:
You are to assume the role of regional director of BRICKYARD PIZZA CO., a carryout pizza chain with forty-one stores. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked you to recommend what to do about the crew schedule at the company's first store outside its home state.

Brickyard Pizza Co. leads its home region on carryout speed and on a hand-stretched crust that its coupon mailers, its app offers, and the lettering on its storefronts have promoted for twenty years. The new store opened three months ago in a county where the unemployment rate has fallen below three percent, so an hourly worker who leaves can have another job within the week.

The store's manager was promoted after six months and wrote the first schedule alone. The eight crew members who moved from the home state to open the store were given the guaranteed thirty-five-hour weeks their written transfer offers promised, and the newly hired local crew were left with whatever hours remained. The local hires are quitting, and the least experienced crew now closes, where prepared dough and cut toppings are thrown out at the end of most nights.

The vice president (judge) wants a recommendation. Holding the schedule keeps the promise the company put in writing to the crew who moved their families, but the local hires keep leaving, the closing shift stays in the hands of the least experienced crew, and the food thrown out each night keeps rising. Rewriting the schedule to divide hours evenly would keep the local hires and steady the closing shift, but it takes back the thirty-five-hour weeks the transferred crew were promised.

You will present your recommendation to the vice president (judge) in the vice president's (judge) office. The vice president (judge) will begin by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the vice president's (judge) questions, the vice president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of vice president of operations of BRICKYARD PIZZA CO. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the regional director (participant) to recommend what to do about the crew schedule at the company's first store outside its home state. You want to hear how the hours should be divided between the crew who transferred and the local hires, what that does to the food thrown out on the closing shift, and what it does to the store's standing in a county where hourly workers can leave for another job within the week.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Where do we expect to see this six months from now?
What does it mean for the next store we open outside the state?
